title: SERA-Float: A Soft Error Resilient Approximate Floating-Point Computing Format
evidence_span: Selected manuscript Sections III.B–IV.C: fixed-width approximate representation, split Hamming exponent protection, mantissa parity, storage fault injection and synthesized multiplication evaluation.
problem: Approximation error and storage bit flips jointly threaten floating-point accuracy and exception behavior.
method_or_artifact: 32-bit approximate floating-point format reallocating mantissa bits to protected exponent/control fields, eight-bit compressed mantissa, parity and number-type identifiers.
workload_or_benchmark: Image sharpening, Gaussian smoothing, KNN, ResNet-50 DNN and linear SVM; CIFAR-100 stated for classification; modeled single-bit and spatial double-bit storage faults.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Verilog synthesis with Synopsys Design Compiler and NanGate 45nm library at 1.10 V and 25 C; stated 1 ns constraint is not demonstrated timing closure. No measured silicon.
baselines: FP32 application-quality reference; FP16, BF16, FP8 and INT8 format comparisons, with FP8 configuration labeling unresolved
limits: Two exponent flips are corrected only across separate protected halves; mantissa parity detects rather than corrects. Stored word remains 32 bits. Accuracy degrades under faults. Headline metrics withheld pending unrounded energy/per-module accounting, injection and evaluation provenance, and independent review. Synthesized per-multiplication energy is not full-inference energy.
